summary: The v6 fixture and ceremony repairs are present and mechanically checkable: FC-REPLAY-NAMED now expects the typed replay refusal; FC-RECOVERY-AUTHORITY adds distinct reserved-threshold and old-root/new-root/role-binding vectors; ceremonyTermination points to the bounded toFunction result rather than the old computed token; and TRUSTED EV-INSTALL gains an ENVELOPE-INACTIVE branch. Acceptance is still withheld because the contract never defines structured branch precedence over defaultTransition. Every relevant guard requires ACTIVE, defaultTransition still sends a false guard to the event fallback, while the edited fallback notes say whenInactive wins; RECOVER-COMMIT also retains an unqualified whenFailed branch carrying a competing reason. All readings refuse and preserve state, so this is not a blocker, but the exact audit reason remains non-deterministic. Two advisories cover a repeated roster-parenthetical under-description and the now-COMPLETE Codex v5 verdict remaining unpinned as provisional. At 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, DR-112 remains OPEN and this verdict authorizes no implementation.

shouldFix.title: INACTIVE branch precedence remains undefined, so the exact refusal reason is not deterministic
shouldFix.measurement: defaultTransition is byte-identical to v5 and says that if no named member has a true guard, fallbackByEvent applies, including when a named pair's guards are false. Transitions 0-3 and 16 require TRUSTED-entry ACTIVE, so INACTIVE makes their stated guard false. Their whenInactive objects assign ENVELOPE-INACTIVE, but no machine rule says those objects are evaluated before or instead of the guard-false fallback. The revised PRESENT and COMMIT fallback notes merely assert that whenInactive wins; EV-INSTALL's fallback note still says admission is only from TRUSTED while ACTIVE. RECOVER-COMMIT additionally retains a sibling whenFailed object with no ACTIVE qualifier and refusalReason RECOVERY-COMMIT-REFUSED, so an inactive recovery predicate is both whenInactive and failed under the declared text.
shouldFix.whyShouldFix: Every competing interpretation refuses, performs no fetch or lock mutation, and leaves the state unchanged, so there is no fail-open security path and no blocker. But FC-ENVELOPE-INACTIVE requires exactly ENVELOPE-INACTIVE and auditAndWaiver makes the refusal reason a required conformance value. A generated state-machine evaluator cannot choose between named whenInactive, generic whenFailed, and event fallback without inventing precedence that the contract does not state.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define the outcome-branch selection algorithm in machine.defaultTransition or a dedicated discipline field: evaluate mutually exclusive whenInactive / whenActiveFailure / whenActiveSuccess branches on a named member before event fallback, with fallback reached only when no branch matches. Rename or qualify transition 16 whenFailed as ACTIVE-but-other-recoveryTrustedEntry-conjunct-failed, and make the PRESENT, INSTALL, and COMMIT fallback exclusions normative rather than note-only.

advisories.title: The successor roster repeats the parenthetical under-description it claims to fold
advisories.detail: basedOn.method names '/machine/transitions[ST-TRUSTED+EV-INSTALL] (whenInactive)', but v6 adds both whenInactive and whenActiveSuccess. This is the same pattern Claude v5 ADV-1 identified. All 25 changed leaves remain inside rostered parent paths, so the closed-roster boundary is not breached and this stays advisory; either name both children or omit the narrowing parenthetical.
